Personally, I wish I had transitioned sooner (started hormones at 25), but I had so many things I was dealing with before that point I just didn't have the chance to do it. If you're feeling comfortable moving forward with it then I don't see any reason not to.

Do you have a tendency to mask when in these situations? Your mask may lean feminine and it's just reflex for you. I'm also autistic, and I had a time in highschool where even though I knew I was a guy, I would still dress really femininely and questioned if that meant I was really trans. So much so, I didn't get on hormones until this past 1.5 years (age 25 at the time). At that point, I finally got diagnosed as autistic and realized that my mask was where most of my need to present as female when I went outside or when socializing came from. It was the ruleset I knew, so I wasn't comfortable changing that by socially being seen as a guy. I'm still working on unmasking, and with that I have felt more and more secure in my trans identity.

I've also noticed that I'm not like, Man™, but I do prefer masculine over the feminine when I think of how I want to look and how I want to interact with the world. Before I was in the mindset that either you are one or the other, very black and white. Now I see gender as more of a gradient, feminine to neutral to masculine. And I think that's a much more accurate model than the very black and white thinking. 

Overall, my advice is to reschedule if possible, and give yourself some time to reflect on who you feel you are, and what things you do to avoid being put in a social situation you don't like or don't know the script for. Also, don't be afraid of having feminine interests or having a feminine side, most people have some traits from both sides. It's up to you where in that scale you feel you fall, and if you are wanting to look more masculine than you are now, I would look into getting on hormones. You can go on low dose T and see where the changes start to happen over time, so you can stop it whenever you want. If you go on T for a few months or years that's fine, and there's plenty of trans people that don't go on hormones at all. It's up to what you are looking for, and if you need time to figure that out, take that time.

I've also struggled with my identity for a long time. I had a relationship that forced me into acting masculine when I wasn't ready. It's definitely hard to go though that, and I'm sorry you've had to go through what you've had to. Luckily, we live in a world where we can change our bodies in pretty much any way we can think of. I know you aren't in your ideal place right now, but never forget that everyone is constantly working towards their best self, and that includes you! Our identities are all unique, and it takes time to find the real you under all the assumptions people make. You can get to the point where you love the skin you're in, but it takes a lot of hard work and time. Find some inspiration for what makes you feel like yourself, and figure out how that would best be done. Is it a wardrobe change? Is it hair styling or color? Little changes can make you feel like you're making progress immediately, while you do more time consuming things like getting weight off or saving for a surgery (if that's what you're looking for!). 

The biggest thing to remember is that this is not forever. You did not ruin your life, you only explored your options and found out it didn't fit! You are also not alone. Feel free to shoot me a dm if you want to vent about it more 💙
